newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares edge higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares edge higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Thursday in thin trading as traders said the market had found a new equilibrium after a decline of five percent since the beginning of the week.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.17 percent, or 0.42 points, to 253.14 on low all-share turnover of 127 million shekels against 146 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.05 percent lower at 261.36.

"The market has reached an equilibrium despite the political uncertainty. The market was mixed and it seems like its stabilising at the current level," said Daniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"The market is very stable and investors are waiting for political developments in the Bar-On story and Har Homa. The fact that activity was low shows that the market is in a waiting pattern," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and officials in his government are being questioned by police in connection with charges that the short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general was part of a deal for a plea bargain in the corruption trial of Aryeh Deri, a key figure in the governing coalition.

Meanwhile, a ministerial committee approved on Wednesday the building of 6,500 homes for Jews on Har Homa, a Jerusalem hill taken by Israel in the 1967 war. Palestinians and Israeli leftists have warned the plan could ignite Arab rage.
"Since December the market has risen sharply with no correction. It came a long way in a short time. The latest political events were only a catalyst for the much needed consolidation," Finn said.
"It is only natural that after such a rise the market declines. Foreign investors are still very active and the shares that are identified with them rose today," Hoffman said.
Agan Chemical Manufacturers, the main loser on the Maof and the third most-active issue, plunged 4.75 percent to 7,348 agorot on volume of 5.4 million shekes.
The company on Wednesday reported that earnings fell in the fourth quarter of 1996 to $0.16 a share from $0.24 a year earlier. Traders said they were below expectations.
Agan's parent company Makhteshim Chemical Works fell 3.25 percent to 1,831 agorot.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 21,106 agorot on volume of 13.5 million shekels, and Super Sol, which surged 4.5 percent to 1,046 agorot on turnover of 6.3 million shekels.
